notes: North Tyneside does not run selective or additional licensing. Only large HMOs need a licence: five or more people in two or more households. The council's Private Sector Housing Plan says it will keep the need for selective and additional licensing under review.
research: DECISIVE PRIMARY SOURCE: North Tyneside's Private Sector Housing Plan 2023-2028, Appendix 1 (2024-25 Delivery Programme), lists as a future action 'Keep under review the need for selective and additional licensing in the borough'. A council keeping under review the NEED for both regimes does not operate either. The same appendix shows what it did instead: 'Introduce a landlord accreditation scheme, initially focussing on Wallsend regeneration area'. FEE TEST: the live HMO page states 'If you rent out a home to five or more people from two or more families, you might need a House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) licence from us' and its fee table reads 'HMO Application Fee: 450 / HMO Licence Fee up to 5 Units: 300 / Additional Licence Fee (per unit above 5): 32 / Change of Managing Agent: 250 / Amendment of Licence: 50'. Mandatory bands only, no Part 3 or s.56 line. NAVIGATION TEST: the Private Sector Housing hub lists only safe warm and healthy homes, empty and derelict properties, advice and support, enforcement, leaseholder information and multiple occupancy homes. /selective-licensing and /housing/private-sector-housing/selective-licensing both return 404. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'Additional Licence Fee (per unit above 5): 32' is a per-unit surcharge on a mandatory licence, NOT s.56. This is the single most misleading line on the site. (2) Landlord accreditation is explicitly labelled 'Voluntary scheme for North Tyneside landlords'. (3) The page also recites the s.254 definition (three or more people from two or more households) while the licensable threshold on the same page is five or more. (4) Neighbour bleed guarded against: nothing from Newcastle upon Tyne, which does have schemes, was used. LIMITATIONS, stated honestly: North Tyneside's sitewide search is broken, returning 'Cannot search on a disabled index', so its nil return proves nothing and carried no weight. There is no sitemap.xml (404 on all variants; robots.txt declares none), so the full-URL sweep used on other councils was impossible. The ModernGov document search ignores GET parameters, returning byte-identical 11,892-byte responses for 'selective licensing' and for the control 'houses in multiple occupation', so committee papers could not be full-text searched. The finding rests on the council's own plan wording plus the fee schedule and navigation. This is the thinnest record in batch 10: solid, but not bulletproof.

notes: North Warwickshire does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for five or more unrelated people sharing facilities. A borough-wide Article 4 direction from 2 March 2026 means new HMOs need planning permission, which is separate from licensing.
research: COUNCIL SELF-DECLARATION. The HMO Article 4 Report to the Planning and Development Board, 6 October 2025, section 6, contains a comparator table whose North Warwickshire row reads: 29 HMO licences, 27,580 households, 0.44 licensed HMOs per 1000 population, 'Additional Scheme: No', 'Selective Licensing: No'. That is the council stating its own position in a published committee paper. FEE TEST: the HMO page states 'You need a mandatory HMO licence if: five or more unrelated people live at the property and all or some of them share a toilet, bathroom or kitchen' and 'HMO licences are usually granted for five years.' The fee table is headed 'Mandatory HMO licence Fees': New Application 5-9 £904, 10-14 £952, 15-19 £1000, 20+ £1046; Renewal £833 / £870 / £907 / £944. Every band keys to the mandatory five-plus threshold; no Part 3 or s.56 line. SEARCH TEST: the site search is server-side, honours quoted phrases and reports counts. '"selective licensing"' returned 'Results 1 - 5 of about 5' and '"additional licensing"' returned 'Results 1 - 3 of about 3'. All eight hits are the comparator table, civil-penalty boilerplate, a CON29O conveyancing form and LACORS fire guidance. SITEMAP TEST: 5,923 URLs pulled, ZERO contain 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED, one severe: (1) ARTICLE 4. North Warwickshire confirmed a BOROUGH-WIDE HMO Article 4 Direction taking effect 2 March 2026. The sealed direction was read in full: made under article 4(1) of the GPDO 2015, First Schedule withdrawing permitted development for 'change of use of a building from a use falling within Class C3 (dwellinghouses) ... to a use falling within Class C4 (houses in multiple occupation)', Second Schedule 'Land being the area of North Warwickshire Borough as shown edged red', 'confirmed and shall take effect on 2 March 2026'. The document contains ZERO occurrences of the word 'licens'. Brand new, borough-wide and future-dated, so it reads exactly like a designation. It is planning control. Highest-risk false positive in this batch. (2) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, also severe: para 6.3 of the council's own report says 'Coventry City have in place an Article 4 Direction restricting HMO's in certain areas and have an Additional Licensing Scheme for small HMO's which took effect May 2025.' A domain-scoped keyword scrape of northwarks.gov.uk returns that sentence and could be misread as North Warwickshire having a scheme. It is Coventry's. The same table also shows Oadby and Wigston with selective 'Yes' and Warwick District with additional 'Yes', both hosted on North Warwickshire's site. (3) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the enforcement procedure lists 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [Section 95 Housing Act 2004]' and, explicitly conditional, 'Offences in relation to the licensing of HMOs or houses if Selective Licensing is in force'. SHARED SERVICE: Nuneaton and Bedworth accepts licence applications for both authorities. Both were verified separately and neither has a designation. LIMITATIONS: general web search was unavailable and external engines were bot-blocked, so no external index cross-check for an orphan page outside the sitemap. Committee agendas were not paged back to 2006.

notes: North West Leicestershire does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for properties with five or more people who are not a single household. Fees are £410 on application and a further £537 before the licence is issued.
research: The council's Housing Enforcement Policy, under 'The Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation', states 'Mandatory requirements for licensing apply only to houses (or flats) that are in multiple occupation' and then 'The Council has discretionary powers to introduce licensing for other residential accommodation through additional or selective licensing schemes.' The construction 'has discretionary powers to INTRODUCE' describes an unexercised power; no designated area, commencement date or fee appears anywhere. FEE TEST: the licence page states 'A property needs a mandatory HMO licence if it is both: A HMO [and] Occupied by five people or more who do not form a single household', then 'There is an initial fee of £410.00 payable with the submission of the application' and 'If an officer intends to grant a licencse, a further fee of £537.00 will be required before the licence is issued' (council's own typo). Two fee lines, both mandatory. COMMITTEE TEST: the ModernGov search works but ONLY via POST with the full hidden field set plus a Referer header; a GET silently returns the blank form, which would look like a false nil return. Driven correctly, '"selective licensing"' returned 6 documents (2019 Cabinet HMO policy, 2023 scrutiny and cabinet private sector housing policies, three Audit and Governance boilerplate items) and '"additional licensing"' returned ZERO. No designation report exists in the committee record. SITEMAP TEST: 923 URLs, ZERO contain 'selective'; the sitemap does include the HMO and landlord pages, so coverage is genuine rather than thin. PIPELINE CHECK: the landlord services consultations page states 'There are no policies currently under review', last updated 22 June 2026. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4 at Kegworth (confirmed 23 July 2020, in force 19 February 2021, whole village, C3 to C4). Planning, not licensing. (2) Neighbour bleed: Leicester City has selective licensing; nothing from Leicester City was attributed here. (3) Civil-penalty boilerplate: 'Section 95 - Offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 (inc. selective licensing)'. (4) Generic legal-framework description: the 2019 Cabinet HMO Licensing Policy lists all three regimes as 'the different types of licenses introduced in the Housing Act 2004', a textbook summary; the recommendation adopted only mandatory fees, room sizes, civil penalties and banning orders. (5) NAMING TRAP: 'Landlord Services Consultations' means the council acting as social landlord to its own tenants, not private rented licensing. (6) Voluntary accreditation via EMLAS. LIMITATIONS: the council's own site search sits behind a JavaScript bot gate and returns no server-side results, so its nil return carried no weight. No reachable consolidated corporate fees schedule exists, so the published HMO service-page fees were used, which are the operative charges. General web search was unavailable.

notes: Norwich does not run selective or additional licensing. Only large HMOs need a licence, where five or more people live in more than one household. Smaller shared houses must still meet safety and management standards but do not need a licence.
research: Norwich's HMO licensing FAQs state: 'Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004 requires Norwich City Council to license certain HMOs in the private rented sector. Licensing was introduced in April 2006 ... In October 2018, the definition of HMO requiring a licence was extended by the Secretary of State to include HMOs with five or more occupants.' Part 2 mandatory only, with no Part 3 anywhere. On the requirement: 'You will require a licence for an HMO when all of the following apply: ... it is occupied by five or more people (including children).' The overview page says 'If the property is home to five or more people, it must be licensed under the national mandatory scheme' and, DECISIVELY AGAINST s.56, 'Safety Standards: we enforce rules around fire safety, electrical checks, and proper amenities - even for HMOs that don't require a licence.' If additional licensing were designated, sub-five HMOs WOULD require a licence; Norwich states they do not. FEE TEST: 'The HMO licence application fee is £1,141, split into two parts: [£636] ... £505 payable once your application has been processed (this covers a 5-year licence)'. A single mandatory fee, no Part 3 or s.56 cost-recovery line. STRUCTURAL TEST: the Licensing section index lists only animal activity, other regulatory licences, pavement, premises and alcohol, taxi and private hire, plus HMOs; 'other regulatory licences' covers street trading, skin piercing, sex establishments, gambling and charitable collections only. /selective-licensing returns 404 and the sitemap contains no 'selective' URL. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS) (England) Regulations 2007' is cited in the FAQs for converted flats. Despite the word 'Additional' this is a management-standards instrument, NOT s.56. (2) The 2025 news item 'Council consulting on updated multiple-occupation housing policy' is a consultation on the ADMINISTRATION of the existing mandatory scheme, not a new designation. It states plainly 'It is only large HMOs that need a licence', and the listed changes are simpler administration, more detail on required information, 'removal of the one- and three-year licence options, all licences will now be five-year licences', and a risk-based approach to breaches. A consultation on a licensing POLICY is not a designation. (3) The closed-consultation register includes an 'Article 4 direction offices residential' item, which is office-to-residential planning control, unrelated to HMOs. LIMITATIONS: Norwich's sitewide search is fuzzy and does not honour quoted phrases; 'selective licensing' returned 141 pages led by allotment policies and a tenants' magazine article about drones, so it is worthless as a nil test and carried no weight. cmis.norwich.gov.uk returned 403 and norwich.moderngov.co.uk returned 522, so committee papers could not be searched. The published sitemap holds only 335 URLs, which is small for the site, so it may not be exhaustive. I could not locate a current Norwich HMO Article 4 page on the rebuilt site and am not asserting Norwich's Article 4 position either way; it does not affect the licensing verdict.

notes: Nuneaton and Bedworth does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for properties let to five or more people in two or more households. A councillor working group has been looking at selective licensing, but no scheme has been made.
research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE, with an active but preliminary member-level discussion that has produced no designation. FEE TEST: the HMO page states 'Any property, regardless of the number of storeys, that is let to five or more people, in two or more households, who share amenities such as bathroom and kitchen, will require a house in multiple occupation (HMO) licence from the local authority.' Fees: '£841 where the house is occupied by five persons living as two or more households', '£882 for six to ten occupiers', '£923 for eleven occupiers and over'. All three bands key to the mandatory threshold; no Part 3 or s.56 line. SEARCH TEST, and this one is meaningful: the site search reports counts and passed a control test. The control query 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 'about 115' results including the real HMO pages, so the engine indexes the site properly. The single word 'selective' returned only 'about 19' results, every distinct one enumerated and disposed of. SITEMAP TEST: 6,468 URLs, ZERO contain 'selective'. /private-housing/selective-licensing returns 404, and the private housing index lists only caravan and mobile home licensing, drainage, empty properties, energy grants, HMO, illegal eviction, energy efficiency standards, overcrowding, smoke and CO detectors, and unauthorised encampments. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NATIONAL MODEL FORM: the HMO Licence Application Pack contains 'or selective licensing under the Housing Act 2004' in the fit-and-proper-person declaration, standard national wording present in every council's form. (2) OPTIONS PAPER, NOT A SCHEME: the Housing and Communities Overview and Scrutiny Panel report of 23 January 2025 explains both regimes generically and is conditional throughout: 'It should be noted that if the council decided to introduce additional or selective licensing, such schemes would only be introduced for a maximum period of 5 years'. The same report confirms the current position: 'Currently HMOs with three or four tenants ... do not require a license'. (3) WORKING GROUP, INFORMATION-GATHERING ONLY: a minute of 22 January 2026 records 'Russ Dyable (Rent-a-Room) be invited to the next meeting of the Working Group to provide information on selective licensing conditions', repeated as an outstanding action in an April 2026 tracker. Inviting an external speaker to brief members is not a proposal, not a statutory consultation and not a designation. There is no published proposal, no consultation, no designated area and no fee. (4) IRRELEVANT WORD MATCHES: the Shopfronts and Advertisement Design Guide policy AD7 ('The selective use of mounted signs') and a September 2025 planning report ('being selective in the evidence base documents'). (5) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: Coventry has an additional licensing scheme for small HMOs from May 2025; nothing from Coventry was attributed here. SHARED SERVICE: the council accepts licence applications for both Nuneaton and Bedworth and North Warwickshire properties. Both authorities were verified independently and neither has a designation. LIMITATIONS: the ModernGov portal returned 522 and apps.nuneatonandbedworth.gov.uk did not resolve, so committee papers were reached only through indexed site search and direct PDF downloads. General web search was unavailable.

notes: Pendle does not currently run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for five or more tenants forming more than one household. Pendle designated selective licensing areas in the past, but the most recent proposals date from 2017 and have since lapsed.
research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE for the current position, with a genuine expired history. This was the highest-prior council in the batch (mill-town terraced stock in Nelson, Brierfield and Colne) and was dug into rather than accepting a quick nil. FEE TEST: the 'Do I need a licence?' page describes mandatory licensing ONLY: pre-October 2018 'at least 3 storeys high' with 'at least 5 tenants' forming 'more than 1 household' sharing 'toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities', extended from 1 October 2018 to 'all HMOs with 5 or more tenants, making up 2 or more households, and which share some facilities' regardless of storeys. Fees: 'Application fee of £590' and 'Licence fee of £296' (total £886), and 'The licence is valid for five years'. No selective or s.56 line. NAVIGATION TEST: the Landlords section lists 18 items covering energy efficiency, possession, deposits, ASB, rent arrears, safety topics and HMOs, with NO selective licensing entry. The A-Z under 'S' lists sandbags through street trading with no selective licensing entry. SEARCH TEST, done carefully because Pendle's search misbehaves: the quoted-phrase search is BROKEN, returning 0 results for '"selective licensing"' but ALSO 0 for the control phrase '"houses in multiple occupation"' which demonstrably exists on the site, so that nil return was discarded entirely. The unquoted search does OR matching (710 results dominated by Licensing Act 2003 and taxi content), equally useless. The discriminating test was the SINGLE WORD 'selective', which returned exactly 4 results: Information 0, Downloads 0, Services 0, News 0, Meeting Minutes 4. Zero live service pages anywhere on the site. SITEMAP TEST: 11,252 URLs, ZERO contain 'selective'. HISTORY: the four hits are all archived Executive attachments: 'Item 4 Selective Licensing' (22 January 2015), 'Item 14 Selective Licensing Update' (22 October 2015), 'Item 12 Proposed Selective Licensing for the Waterside Area (including Appendices)' (17 March 2016), and 'Item 11 Proposed Colne Selective Licensing Area' plus 'Item 11 Revised Appendix 3 - List of Streets' (16 March 2017). The most recent is March 2017. A Part 3 designation lasts a maximum of five years, so even a scheme commenced immediately after that report would have expired by 2022, and nothing appears in the committee record since. No expired scheme object was recorded because confirmed commencement and end dates could not be established from the committee index alone. TRAPS EXCLUDED: expired-schemes-presented-as-live is precisely the risk here and was avoided by dating the last committee activity; neighbour bleed guarded against, as Burnley borders Pendle and nothing from Burnley was used. LIMITATIONS: the archived committee attachment pages expose only document titles and file sizes, not extractable text, so the Waterside and Colne designation instruments could not be read to confirm exact commencement and expiry dates. The finding is that nothing is live today, which is what a landlord needs; precise historical dates are not asserted. NOTE FOR THE DATASET: Pendle's historic designations were street-based (the Colne report carried a 'List of Streets' appendix) rather than ward-based, so they would not have been ward-matchable in any event.

notes: Plymouth does not run selective or additional licensing. Only large HMOs need a licence, where at least five people live in more than one household. Plymouth has an Article 4 direction requiring planning permission to convert a house to a small HMO in some areas, which is separate from licensing.
research: Plymouth initially returned HTTP 403 to every request; per method that was treated as a bot block rather than evidence and retried with a browser user-agent via curl, which got straight through. The 403 was indeed a block. FEE TEST, decisive: the HMO licence application page carries the complete published schedule under 'Cost': 'Initial Application (Full Fee) £1,097', 'Initial Application (discounted fee for holding accreditation) £982', 'Renewal Application (Full Fee) £1,040', 'Renewal Application (discounted fee for holding accreditation) £924'. The page opens 'To reduce sharing problems and to ensure multiple occupancy homes are of a decent standard, landlords need a licence for a large House in Multiple Occupation (HMO).' Large HMOs only. No Part 3 line, no s.56 line, no per-property private-rented licensing fee. LICENSABILITY TEST: the HMO page states 'A HMO is likely to be licensable if all of the following apply: At least 5 people live there forming more than one household [and] It is a HMO'. NAVIGATION TEST: the landlords hub links only to Houses in Multiple Occupation, Private rented accommodation safety, Rent a room in your home and Renters' Rights Act 2025. SITEMAP TEST, the strongest structural evidence: the sitemap index and all three sub-sitemaps were pulled, 5,899 URLs in total, and ZERO contain 'selective'. The only property-licensing URLs on the entire domain are /houses-multiple-occupation-hmo, /apply-house-multiple-occupation-hmo-licence, /hmo-standards, /hmo-register-and-unlicenced-hmos, /standards-and-managing-hmo and /planning-permission-and-houses-multiple-occupation-hmo. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4, confirmed present exactly as warned. The planning page states 'In some areas and for specific buildings we've removed these rights by introducing an Article 4 Direction ... This means you'll have to apply for planning permission if you want to change a house (C3) to a small HMO (C4) in the following neighbourhoods', with a named-neighbourhood list and an areas map. It names neighbourhoods and carries commencement, so it reads like a designation, but it is permitted-development control and NOT Housing Act licensing. (2) THE s.254 DEFINITION, present on the same site and the classic conflation risk: the HMO page opens 'A building, or part of a building, is likely to be a House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) if both of the following apply: at least 3 people live there, forming more than one household [and] they share a toilet, bathroom or kitchen'. That is the definition; the licensable threshold, stated separately on the same page, is at least five people. (3) The accreditation discount on the fee table is a voluntary-scheme discount on a mandatory licence, not a separate regime. LIMITATIONS: Plymouth's Drupal site search is fuzzy and stemmed and cannot deliver a meaningful nil return; the single word 'selective' returned 97 results led by 'Library market day at St Budeaux Library' and a procurement climate statement, so it carried no weight and the sitemap sweep was relied on instead. democracy.plymouth.gov.uk failed TLS certificate verification, so committee papers could not be full-text searched; a very recent cabinet report proposing a future designation would not necessarily have surfaced, though it would not change a landlord's obligation today.

notes: Redditch does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for properties occupied by at least five people in two or more households who share an amenity. The fee is £163.90 per person and a licence lasts up to five years.
research: The landlords page states 'To be a licensable HMO the property must be occupied by at least 5 persons who comprise of two or more households and share at least one basic amenity such as a bathroom or kitchen' and 'The HMO licence is usually issued for a period of up to 5 years and the fee is £163.90 per person.' A single mandatory per-person fee with no selective or s.56 counterpart anywhere on the site. CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy, section 8 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licensing', describes mandatory licensing only, with no Part 3, selective, additional or designation anywhere in the document. SHARED-SERVICE RISK CLEARED: Worcestershire Regulatory Services was checked and ruled out as a possible holder of a scheme. The WRS licensing index covers alcohol and entertainment, animals, pavement, taxi, tax conditionality, gambling and public registers, with NO housing or HMO licensing at all. Redditch's own Private Sector Housing Team runs housing licensing. BROMSGROVE KEPT SEPARATE: Bromsgrove publishes a different fee, '£156.80 per person', on the same mandatory five-person test with no scheme. The distinct figures confirm the two authorities were not conflated in either direction. FEE-SCHEDULE CAVEAT, stated honestly: the corporate Licensing fees and charges 2026-2027 PDF (9 pages, text extracted) contains NO housing or HMO line at all, covering only taxi and private hire, animal activity, zoo, dangerous wild animals, skin piercing, gambling, street trading, scrap metal, sex establishments, pavement licences and hypnotism. Housing fees sit outside that schedule, so its silence is weak evidence and is not the basis of this finding. The probative fee is the single £163.90 per person mandatory figure. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) s.254 definition: the resident-facing HMO page says 'at least 3 tenants live there, forming more than 1 household', while the licensing pages state five or more. (2) A STALE MANDATORY TEST: the enforcement policy still says 'HMOs of three or more storeys, with five or more occupants require a licence', which is the pre-October 2018 wording. That indicates an out-of-date document, not an additional licensing scheme. (3) 'HMO Grants - £25k' in the 2025-26 Financial Plan capital programme is a landlord grant budget line, not a scheme. (4) 'Additional' used as a surcharge word in unrelated fees, e.g. 'Private hire operator licence (per additional vehicle)'. LIMITATIONS: Redditch's own site search is BROKEN and its nil return was discarded; it returned 'No results match your search' for 'selective licensing' and ALSO for the control term 'HMO', despite HMO pages plainly existing. Committee papers were unreachable: moderngov.redditchbc.gov.uk and moderngov.bromsgroveandredditch.gov.uk do not resolve in DNS, and redditch.moderngov.co.uk returned 403. General web search was unavailable and external engines were bot-blocked; because the DuckDuckGo control query never completed, its apparent nil return was not treated as evidence. Residual risk is a designation made very recently and not yet reflected on the website or in the fees.

notes: Reigate and Banstead does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for properties housing five or more people in two or more households who share facilities. The current fee is £1,082 per property for a five-year licence.
research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE, high confidence, resting on a complete published fee schedule. THRESHOLD: the HMO page states 'HMOs which accommodate five or more persons in two or more households (sharing facilities) require a licence, irrespective of the number of storeys in the building.' FEE TEST, decisive: every row of the 2026/2027 environmental health fees and charges table was captured. The only licensing rows relevant to rented housing are 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) | Five yearly - per property (new application) | £1082 | Licence' and 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) | Five yearly - per property (renewal) | £1082 | Licence'. The remainder is EIR requests, food hygiene revisits, Mobile Home Sites (16 rows), Private Water Supply and Property Inspections. There is NO selective, Part 3, additional or private rented sector licensing row in the current published schedule. A live Part 3 or s.56 scheme is required to be self-financing and would have to carry its own cost-recovery fee; none exists. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, the main risk for this council: Croydon operates borough-wide schemes and directly adjoins Reigate and Banstead. No Croydon material was used or relied on, and the same applies to Epsom and Ewell, Mole Valley, Tandridge and Crawley. (2) 'Property Inspections | Officer Time for Housing Act Enforcement | £65 | Per hour' and 'Formal Notices | £486 | Per notice' are HHSRS enforcement cost recovery under Part 1 of the Housing Act 2004, not a licensing scheme. (3) Mobile Home Sites licensing, including a 'Fit and Proper Person' fee, sits under the Caravan Sites and Control of Development Act and the Mobile Homes Act 2013. A separate regime, neither Part 2 nor Part 3. (4) The £65 register copy fee is administrative. The register itself 'does not distinguish between mandatory, additional, or selective licences', so it is neutral evidence and was not read as positive. (5) 'Landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) also have additional responsibilities relating to the management of their property' uses 'additional' in a management sense, not s.56. LIMITATIONS: reigate-banstead.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 403 on every path attempted, so cabinet reports could not be scanned. No working site-search endpoint could be found (/search and /search/ both 404), and the consultations pages returned placeholder or mismatched content, so consultation history could not be swept for a proposed-but-never-designated scheme. General web search was unavailable and all external engines were bot-blocked; a DuckDuckGo nil return was obtained but its control query never completed, so it was not treated as evidence. Residual risk is a very recent designation not yet reflected on the site or in the 2026/2027 fees. Noted in passing that Reigate and Banstead is currently running a Community Governance Review and a Local Government Reorganisation process, which would become relevant to ward matching only if a designation were ever made.

notes: Ribble Valley does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for properties occupied by five or more people in two or more households who share amenities. The total fee is about £1,589, with a 20% discount for accredited landlords.
research: This is 'we checked and found nothing' plus a positive fee-schedule test, not an affirmative council denial, because Ribble Valley publishes no equivalent of Rochford's explicit statement. THRESHOLD: the only HMO page on the site states 'From 1 October 2018 the rules around HMO licensing will change ... a landlord must apply for a licence for a privately rented HMO if the property being rented out' is 'occupied by five or more people' forming 'two or more households' sharing amenities, with 'Purpose built apartment blocks consisting of three or more apartments will not require a licence.' FEE TEST: the live Fees and Charges 2026/2027 schedule, 37 pages, Environmental Health ENVHT ledger, page 24, under 'Houses of Multiple Occupation Licences **', reads: 'HMO Licence Part 1 fee - Processing a licence application for either 2 years or 5 years ... 995.70 [2025] 1,020.60 [2026]'; 'HMO Licence Part 2 fee - Licence scheme running costs, including compliance monitoring ... 554.30 [2025] 568.20 [2026]'; 'Variation of an HMO Licence ... 171.10 [2025] 175.40 [2026]'; footnote '** If licence applicant is a member of a recognised landlord scheme, there is a 20% reduction'. Approximate current mandatory total £1,588.80 from 1 April 2026. There is NO Part 3, selective or additional licensing fee line anywhere in the 37-page schedule. CORROBORATION: the Licensing A-Z index lists 16 licence types (alcohol, animal welfare, busking, caravans, gambling, hackney carriage, hypnotists, pavement, scrap metal, sex establishments, street trading, tattooing, zoo and others) with NO HMO or property licensing entry at all. The application form is titled 'LICENCE APPLICATION - To Operate a House of Multiple Occupation under the Provisions of the Housing Act 2004, Part 2'. Part 2 only. The public HMO register lists roughly 10 properties, all with 4 to 8 sleeping rooms and maximum occupancies of 5 to 14, consistent with the mandatory threshold. SITEMAP TEST: 37,588 URLs, ZERO contain 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NATIONAL MODEL FORM: the application form says you must tell relevant persons 'whether this is an application under Part 2 (Houses in Multiple Occupation) or Part 3 (selective licensing of other properties) of the Housing Act 2004'. Statutory notification wording present in every council's form. (2) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: the 20% reduction for 'a member of a recognised landlord scheme' is an accreditation discount. (3) ARTICLE 4: four exist, at 1-5 The Grove (15 September 2011), Grove House (26 May 2011) and Clitheroe town centre shopping frontage (1991). All planning, none HMO-related. (4) 'Whalley - Designation Approval' superficially reads like a licensing designation; it sits inside download record 244 'Neighbourhood Planning' alongside 'Whalley - Proposal for Neighbourhood Plan' and 'Whalley - Area Plan', so it is a neighbourhood plan area designation. (5) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, the main risk here: Ribble Valley borders Burnley, Pendle, Hyndburn, Preston and Blackburn with Darwen, several of which have or have had selective licensing. Everything above comes from ribblevalley.gov.uk. LIMITATIONS: the committee portal search is unusable, returning byte-identical 13,114-byte responses for 'selective licensing', 'additional licensing' and 'houses in multiple occupation', so it serves the blank form and ignores GET keywords. Committee papers could not be full-text searched, and an 'approved but never commenced' decision would not necessarily have surfaced. notes: Rochford does not run selective or additional licensing, and the council states these are not currently considered appropriate for the district. Only mandatory HMO licences are needed, for five or more people in two or more households. Fees start at £423.92 for up to five bedrooms.
research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE with an explicit, dated, primary-source denial of both regimes, the strongest evidence in this batch. The Rochford District Council Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Civil Penalties Policy, Version 1, 2024 (43 pages) states around page 35: 'The Housing Act 2004 allows for the introduction of Selective Licensing Schemes and Additional Licensing Schemes. These are not currently considered appropriate to be adopted within Rochford, but this matter will be kept under review.' In the same document's civil-penalty offence list, the usual Part 3 boilerplate is annotated by the council itself: 'Offences in relation to selective licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Act (section 95 of the Housing Act 2004) (Rochford does not currently have a selective licensing designation in place)'. THRESHOLD: the licensing page states 'Rochford District Council operate a mandatory licensing scheme only as per the legislation below which came into force October 2018', citing the Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Description) (England) Order 2018 and the five-or-more persons in two-or-more households test. FEE TEST: under the heading 'Mandatory licensing': 'Up to 5 bedrooms £423.92', 'For each additional bedroom £66.55', 'Renewal of Licence 50% of the Fee'. Mandatory bands only. SITEMAP TEST: 959 URLs, ZERO contain 'selective', and no additional-licensing page exists. The only property-licensing pages are /houses-in-multiple-occupation-hmo, /licensing-for-certain-hmos, /applying-for-a-hmo-licence, /standards-required-in-hmos and /register-of-licenced-hmo-in-the-rochford-district. CURRENCY: the public HMO register lists 10 licensed properties, 'Last updated 25 February 2026', and the temporary exemption notice register shows a notice first issued 22 April 2026 (42-46 Eastwood Road, Rayleigh), so these pages are actively maintained in 2026 rather than stale. BRENTWOOD SHARED-SERVICE RISK CLEARED: Rochford's private sector housing and HMO pages are live and self-hosted, with a 2026-updated register and a Rochford-branded 2024 enforcement policy naming the Rochford Private Sector Housing team. No migration of housing pages to Brentwood was found. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the s.95 Part 3 offence line appears as it does in every council's policy; here Rochford annotates it with its own denial, but it would have been excluded regardless. (2) 'For each additional bedroom £66.55' is a per-room surcharge on the mandatory licence, NOT s.56. (3) Neighbour bleed: nothing from Southend-on-Sea, Castle Point, Basildon, Chelmsford or Maldon was attributed to Rochford. (4) No Article 4 hits were found on the Rochford estate. LIMITATIONS: Rochford's own site search is unusable and its nil return proves nothing; a quoted search for 'selective licensing' returned an empty results template, but so did the CONTROL query for 'mandatory licensing', a phrase that demonstrably appears on their own HMO pages, so the search simply does not honour the parameter. rochford.moderngov.co.uk/mgSearch.aspx returned 403 on two attempts, so committee papers could not be full-text searched. General web search was unavailable and external engines were bot-blocked. Residual risk here is near zero given the council's own explicit statement in its current policy.
